chains.title: Supervised mobile verification for fixed-camera blind spots

scene.statement: An alert or prolonged absence creates a need to check another room
scene.rationale: The decision is triggered by an observable verification gap, not by a general interest in mobile devices
assumptions: The synthetic alert and absence scenes represent the pilot's intended use boundary
scene.trigger: An unusual-noise alert or two hours without a camera sighting while away
scene.environment: Away from home with fixed-camera blind spots
scene.task_context: Inspect the relevant space before deciding whether intervention is needed

user.statement: Remote pet owners whose current cameras leave important blind spots
user.rationale: Only owners with an unverified blind-spot scene have the observed problem; satisfied full-coverage owners are a control
assumptions: The owner is also the pilot purchase and intervention decision-maker
user.role: Remote pet owners whose current cameras leave important blind spots
user.state: Away from home and unable to verify the pet in the current camera view
user.decision_role: Pet owner deciding whether to intervene and whether to join the pilot

pain.statement: Fixed cameras and neighbor requests cannot verify blind spots quickly enough
pain.rationale: The selected users' current substitutes fail in the identified scene and produce a delayed or unnecessary intervention
assumptions: The observed delay and social cost matter enough to justify a bounded pilot
pain.current_substitute: Fixed cameras or asking a neighbor
pain.friction_cost: Blind spots, additional installation, or a slow and socially costly neighbor request

need.statement: Verify a blind spot promptly without an unnecessary return home or expanded always-on recording
need.rationale: The pain implies a solution-neutral verification outcome; it does not by itself prove that mobile hardware is the right answer
assumptions: Prompt remote verification is valuable even when no intervention follows
need.desired_outcome: Determine whether intervention is needed before returning home or asking a neighbor
constraints: Avoid routine dependence on a neighbor
need.measure: Time to a verification decision and unnecessary return or neighbor requests avoided in a bounded pilot

feature.statement: A session-bounded mobile check with explicit privacy controls
feature.rationale: On-demand movement addresses the blind-spot need while session, shutter and room boundaries answer the observed privacy rejection
assumptions: Privacy controls remain understandable and effective outside the prototype setting
feature.capability: Move to a blind spot only during an explicit supervised session with physical shutter, room limits and visible recording state

product.rationale: The mobile check and its privacy controls form the smallest coherent pilot that can test the need, solution acceptance and retained behavior together
assumptions: A two-week pilot is sufficient to reject an unusable or unwanted concept, but not to estimate market demand
product.form: Supervised mobile camera device controlled through an explicit bounded session
product.scope: Two-week pilot for on-demand blind-spot verification in approved rooms
non_goals: Replacement for a whole-home security system
acceptance_criteria: Participants complete the blind-spot verification task
Privacy controls are used without unresolved rejection
Predeclared retained-use threshold is met during the pilot

business.statement: Run a bounded paid pilot before making any subscription, launch, or market-expansion decision
business.rationale: The product creates a testable value loop, while a bounded paid pilot is the smallest business experiment that can test payment and retained behavior without pretending to prove a sustainable company
assumptions: A real pilot can recruit eligible owners without changing their privacy or usage behavior
Pilot support and delivery costs can be measured before any scale decision
business.market_definition: Remote pet owners with fixed-camera blind spots in an illustrative urban consumer sample
included_markets: Remote household pet checking through a supervised mobile session
business.target_segment: Owners who cannot verify an important room with their current setup and are eligible for a supervised two-week pilot

segments.criteria: Remote owners with an important fixed-camera blind spot and no satisfactory neighbor alternative
segments.payer: The remote pet owner who reserves the pilot

business.payer: The remote pet owner who reserves and pays a refundable pilot deposit
business.positioning: A privacy-bounded alternative to adding fixed cameras or asking a neighbor; not a whole-home security replacement
business.revenue_model: Refundable pilot deposit only; no subscription or long-term revenue is assumed
business.pricing_hypothesis: Payment behavior is observed only for the synthetic pilot deposit; final pricing and elasticity remain unknown
competitive_alternatives: No change to the current setup

market_estimates.population_definition: Not estimated from the synthetic convenience sample
market_estimates.method: Requires an external sampling frame and paid-demand evidence before estimation

success_metrics.definition: Participants still actively using the bounded check at the end of the pilot
success_metrics.guardrail: Privacy rejection, unresolved support burden, or return rate crosses the predeclared threshold

gate.resource_commitment: Synthetic fixture only; no real budget or launch resource is committed
gate.revisit_trigger: Privacy rejection, task failure, retained-use, or cost threshold fails

alternative_explanations: The current fixed-camera setup may already be adequate for users without blind spots
Privacy concerns may outweigh the value of mobile verification even with the proposed controls

human_review.notes: Illustrates the review contract; no real semantic approval occurred
human_review.risk_acceptance: No real product or launch approval is implied

prioritization.method: Synthetic gate choice: test privacy, acceptance and retained use before any scale decision

factors.consequence: privacy rejection would invalidate the pilot

prioritization.decided_at: Synthetic fixture; no real decision date
prioritization.rationale: The pilot is prioritized as the smallest test that can reverse the concept; no market-size ranking is claimed

change_log.impact: Added privacy controls and bounded product scope
change_log.decision: Keep privacy and retention as predeclared pilot gates
change_log.decided_at: Synthetic fixture; no real decision date

gaps: Privacy controls are not tested in real homes
The feature-to-product rationale still requires a real bounded pilot; evidence completeness does not prove product success
chains.next_test: Run a real two-week bounded pilot with predeclared privacy-rejection, task-success and retained-use thresholds
